evidence: hbnf-guest-controller/hbnf-guest.js render() calls controlsEnabled(open), which enables all Vibe/Arcade/IRL buttons whenever session.open is true
refreshSession() calls applyCapabilities() and then render(), so render() can overwrite the per-capability disabled state
boot() restores a saved session, calls render(), then refreshSession(), so a previously open saved session can temporarily present all controls enabled before fresh status resolves
findings.consequence: Current staging client does not meet the capability-scoped guest UX contract and must not be treated as safe evidence of authorization behavior.
findings.required_resolution: UI must derive each control's enabled state from fresh granted capabilities and default closed during unresolved/stale session state; server remains authoritative on every mutation.

evidence: Current client reads initial ?s= token only for status resolution
Mutation POST body contains sessionId and payload but no defined short-lived verifier/cookie/proof
No production guest backend/authorization endpoint exists in repository search/current status
findings.consequence: Do not connect current client to a mutation backend until session proof/exchange and server-side capability enforcement are explicitly defined.
findings.required_resolution: Initial opaque join reference must resolve into server-recognized short-lived authority; every mutation must be capability-checked server-side. Do not treat a public session identifier alone as authorization.

evidence: guest service worker is registered without an explicit narrower scope
if deployed at site root, default service-worker scope is root and can control other same-origin routes
findings.consequence: A separate guest PWA must not be able to intercept owner/cart/admin routes on the same origin.
findings.required_resolution: Deploy/register guest service worker under a guest-specific path/scope (or isolated origin) and add a regression proving owner routes are outside its control.

evidence: service worker applies network-first/cache-put behavior to every GET it intercepts
fallback returns guest HTML when no cached response exists
no explicit exclusion exists for session/status/dynamic API GET requests
findings.consequence: Session/revocation state must never be served from a generic app-shell cache, and non-document resources must not silently fall back to HTML.
findings.required_resolution: Cache only versioned static app-shell assets; never cache guest authority/session/status responses; navigation fallback must be document-specific.

external_evidence.relevance: session identifiers are authorization-critical; URL-based exchange risks leakage; server-side access control/session binding required
service worker scope defines the range of URLs it controls
caching improves offline behavior but is inappropriate for data that must remain fresh

gate: NO guest backend connection, live mutation bridge, or production deployment until these findings are resolved and acceptance tests exist.
